selection_rule: per multiple, the graded rule with the lowest exploration interval score

EV/EBITDA.name: g05-01 net-cash amplification (EV/EBITDA)
EV/EBITDA.mechanism: EV is equity plus debt minus cash, so the proportional error in EV equals the equity mispricing scaled by equity/EV. For a net-cash firm equity exceeds EV, so any disagreement about the operating business is amplified in EV; for a net-debt firm it is damped. Netting cash against debt (rather than using gross debt/assets as in g04-01) captures the cash-rich firms where EV is a residual and the peer multiple misses most in logs.
EV/EBITDA.compact: EV/EBITDA | base constant | terms log_sales -0.8, ebitda_margin -0.7, net_debt_to_ebitda -0.6 | if net_debt_to_ebitda <= p10 x1.3 | if loss_making x1.3

EV/Sales.name: g05-06 pass-through thin gross margin (EV/Sales)
EV/Sales.mechanism: Firms with very thin gross margins (distributors, contractors, commodity processors) pass most revenue through to suppliers, so value is a small multiple of a thin spread and EV/Sales is roughly proportional to that spread; small absolute differences in gross margin between the target and its peers become large proportional differences in the right EV/Sales, so the peer median misses more in logs. This differs from the low-EBITDA-margin flag because it targets the revenue pass-through structure itself, not current losses.
EV/Sales.compact: EV/Sales | base constant | terms peer_range +0.5, log_sales -0.6 | if gross_margin <= p15 x1.4 | if ebitda_margin <= p15 x1.4 | if n_peers <= p10 x1.4
